course_name_original: Expresión Gráfica y diseño asistido por ordenador
prerequisites: It is recommended to have taken the Technical Drawing course in high school.

learning_outcomes.text: Will master the knowledge and use of applicable standards in industrial drawing

Will master the knowledge of graphic representation techniques for objects, both through traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and through computer-aided design applications.
Will develop the ability and skill in handling manual and computer-aided drawing tools.

Will be able to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, as well as communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of industrial engineering.
Will develop the ability and skill for decision-making in the field of industrial engineering through the study of data obtained by combining graphic and written language.
Will have acquired the ability and skill to correctly reflect decisions in the field of industrial engineering, through the study of data obtained by combining graphic and written language.
Will have acquired the capacity for teamwork, to design and develop simple projects.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Graphic Expression. Definition of Graphic Expression. History of Graphic Expression. Graphic Expression in Engineering. Evolution of Graphic Expression Tools.

Standardization and Industrial Drawing. Generalities on standardization. Types of standards. Standardization organizations. Drawing standards. Types of technical drawings. The title block. Formats. Lettering. Scales. List of elements. Folding of drawings.

Standardized Representation. Orthogonal projection. View systems: Dihedral Views. European and American systems. Criteria for view selection. Types of views. Types of lines. Cuts and sections. Most frequent conventions: adjacent parts, intersections, square ends and openings, symmetrical parts, interrupted views, repetitive elements, details, other conventions.

Standardized Dimensioning. Necessity of dimensioning drawings. Types of dimensioning. General principles. Dimensioning elements. Dimensioning methods. Symbols. Arrangement of dimensions. Special indications (radii, equidistant elements, etc.). Other indications (missing dimensions, particular specifications, etc.). Keyways and notches. Conicity and inclination. Profiles. General dimensioning methodology (example).
Assemblies and Exploded Views. Definitions. Assembly drawing. Element reference. Parts list. Standardized material designation. Exploded view drawing. Drawing numbering. Examples.

Schematics and Diagrams. Simplification of drawings. Schematic symbols. Diagrams: process, flow, engineering. Drawing standards in flow and engineering diagrams. Basic schematics of engineering installations.
New Trends and Multimedia Graphic Presentations.

Activities to be developed in another language: Readings and work on reference materials (various texts, articles, software or others) in English, related to the theoretical content of the subject, as support for developing graphic expression appropriately.
assessment_rules: Students can choose continuous or single assessment. For continuous assessment, components include attendance (10%), individual practice dossier (20%), final group project (20%), and continuous assessment tests (50%, split into 40% theoretical questionnaires and 60% practical tests), with specific participation/submission requirements for each. For single assessment, components are a general exam (60%, split into 40% theoretical and 60% practical), individual practice dossier (20%), and final group project (20%). Both parts of the general exam must be passed (>=5) in the same call, and no grades are carried over between calls or academic years.
